title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche notes, c. 1981). Y is an 'elementary Artin (anabelian) variety', i.e. a successive fibration in hyperbolic curves (a hyperbolic polycurve). X is normal. f, g : X -> Y are dominant morphisms whose induced maps on the étale fundamental group, pi_1(f) and pi_1(g), agree up to an inner automorphism of pi_1(Y). The target statement is f = g; this is the injectivity half of the 'Hom-form' of the anabelian conjecture for dominant maps.

Previous page. Y is mapped by a well-chosen i into a semi-abelian variety G (an extension of an abelian variety by a torus, i.e. a generalized Albanese/Jacobian). Because pi_1(f) and pi_1(g) agree outer-wise, i∘g = tau_u∘(i∘f) for some translation u in G. Using dominance, one shrinks X so that f factors as X --f'--> U --j--> Y. Here U is a non-empty open of Y with U+u ⊂ Y. The map g then factors as j'∘f', where j' : U -> Y is induced by tau_u.

This page.
(1) The hypothesis that pi_1(g) and pi_1(f) agree outer-wise becomes: there is alpha in pi_1(Y) with pi_1(j')(gamma) = int(alpha)(pi_1(j)(gamma)) for all gamma in Im(pi_1(X) --pi_1(f')--> pi_1(U)).
(2) For a dominant morphism of normal varieties this image is an open (finite-index) subgroup of pi_1(U). Grothendieck stresses that this is where dominance is used.
(3) So everything reduces to a rigidity lemma for translations. Let U ≠ ∅ be open in Y and u in G with tau_u(U) ⊂ Y. Let j, j' : U -> Y be y ↦ y and y ↦ y+u. If pi_1(j) and pi_1(j') coincide exteriorly on an open subgroup of pi_1(U), then j = j', i.e. u = 0.
(4) He says frankly that he does not expect to prove this geometrically and will fall back on an arithmetic method (presumably Galois actions over finitely generated fields, as later in the notes). A struck-out passage begins announcing a weakening and generalization of the geometric statement.

Margins. A note says this lemma is no stronger than the conclusion of the corollary itself applied to X = an open U of Y, restricted to an open subgroup of pi_1(U); the lemma is a special case, not a new strengthening. A second note says 'Ça sera plus bas!' ('this will come further down').

The next page then extends the corollary to non-dominant f under hypotheses on centralizers of the image of pi_1(X) in pi_1(Y). This uses the fact that open subgroups of successive extensions of free/surface anabelian profinite groups have trivial centralizer.
errors: The reduction to translations needs Y to sit inside a semi-abelian G via a map i that is an immersion, or at least injective enough. Otherwise i∘g = tau_u(i∘f) does not yield g as the restriction of a translation on Y. For higher-dimensional elementary Artin varieties (e.g. Kodaira-type fibred surfaces) the generalized Albanese map need not be an embedding. The phrase 'bien choisi' on the previous page hints that Grothendieck was aware of this, but the point is not justified on the page.

The deduction from equal outer pi_1-maps to i∘g = tau_u(i∘f) relies implicitly on Hom(Alb(X), G) -> Hom(T(Alb X), T(G)) being injective, and on the generalized Albanese property for normal X. This is standard but unstated.

For curves the lemma is in fact provable geometrically. U+u ⊂ Y forces the closure of Y to be translation-stable, so u is torsion and tau_u gives a finite-order automorphism of Y. A non-trivial automorphism of a hyperbolic curve cannot act by an inner automorphism on an open subgroup of pi_1 (pass to a finite cover and use faithfulness of Aut on H^1 with Z/n coefficients, n ≥ 3, Serre-type lemma). Grothendieck's pessimism about a geometric proof is therefore overstated, at least in dimension 1.

ideas.what: Injectivity of Hom_dom(X,Y) -> Hom_outer(pi_1 X, pi_1 Y) for dominant maps into elementary anabelian varieties (hyperbolic polycurves)
ideas.modern_name: Hom-version of the Grothendieck anabelian conjecture (injectivity part) for hyperbolic polycurves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, letter to Faltings 1983); proofs in various settings by Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki (curves), Hoshi and Sawada (polycurves, 2010s)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), Esquisse d'un programme (as conjecture; no proof)

ideas.what: Reduction via the generalized Albanese/semi-abelian variety: maps with equal pi_1 differ by a translation
ideas.modern_name: rigidity of maps to semi-abelian varieties / Albanese reduction

ideas.what: Image of pi_1 under a dominant morphism of normal varieties is open (finite index)
ideas.modern_name: finite-index image of étale pi_1 for dominant maps

ideas.what: Rigidity lemma: a translation preserving an open of Y that acts by an inner automorphism on an open subgroup of pi_1 must be trivial; Grothendieck chooses an arithmetic rather than geometric proof
ideas.modern_name: faithfulness of outer action / trivial centralizers of open subgroups in anabelian pi_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Mochizuki, Tamagawa (centre-freeness and centralizer results)

missed.claim: An unpublished sketch of the injectivity half of the Hom-conjecture for dominant maps into elementary anabelian varieties. It runs via the generalized Albanese, a reduction to translations, and an announced arithmetic argument. It predates the later literature on polycurves (Hoshi, Sawada), but the strategy itself is standard-looking.
missed.quote: Donc on est ramené à ceci: Soit U ouvert ≠∅ de Y ... alors j = j' i.e. u=0. Franchement, je n'espère pas ... le prouver par voie géométrique - pour ceci je me rabats sur une méthode arithmétique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: Grothendieck had worked out the Albanese/translation reduction for polycurves around 1981. It is not a new result for specialists, since the statement is now known in many cases.

deep.surprise_reason: The page documents Grothendieck actually attempting a proof of part of the anabelian Hom-conjecture for higher-dimensional elementary Artin varieties. The specific Albanese-translation reduction is a nice unpublished detail. The mathematics, however, is standard, and the conclusion is known from later work (Mochizuki, Hoshi, Sawada).
transcription_corrections: First line: likely 'L'hyp. que pi_1(g) ≐ pi_1(f) signifie donc', with the hypothesis written via the factorizations, and the displayed formula likely 'pi_1(j')(gamma) = int(alpha) pi_1(j)(gamma)' rather than f, f'.
'pour tt gamma ∈ Im(pi_1(X) --pi_1(f')--> pi_1(U))': the arrow label is pi_1(f') (the map X -> U), not pi_1(f).
'(ce n'est vrai que pour un morphisme dominant !)' probably reads '(c'est vrai pour un morphisme dominant !)'.
'tel que pi_1(U) [?] ..., tel que bar{pi}_1 U ⊂ Y' should read 'Soit U ouvert ≠∅ de Y, u ∈ G, tels que tau_u U ⊂ Y'.

'(désignant par f, f' les morphismes y -> y et y ↦ y alpha' should read '(désignant par j, j' les morphismes y ↦ y et y ↦ y+u de U dans Y) pi_1(j) et pi_1(j') coïncident extérieurement sur un sous-groupe ouvert de pi_1(U)'.
'alors f = f'' should read 'alors j = j''.
'n.bats sur une méthode arithmétique' is 'rabats'; 'je n'espère pas que j'arriverai à le prouver par voie géométrique'.
Margin likely reads: 'NB ceci n'est pas plus fort que la conclusion du corollaire, appliqué au cas où X est un ouvert U de Y et à un sous-groupe ouvert de pi_1(U)'.
